title: kate-core: pick the innermost indent fold
summary: innermost_fold returns the tightest span that contains a line. The header line and the end line are outside. The test goes in the existing fold tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

definitions.definition:
#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
pub fn innermost_fold(spans: &[FoldSpan], line: u32) -> Option<FoldSpan>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: fold.rs is a private module of view.rs. Its one test module is mod tests. Add the new function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Add innermost_fold with the dead_code attribute above the pub fn. A span contains line when line is greater than start and less than end. Return the containing span with the greatest start. When two containing spans share that start, return the shorter one. Return None when no span contains the line. The test innermost_fold_picks_the_inner_span calls indent_folds on a, newline, two spaces, b, newline, four spaces, c, newline, two spaces, d, newline, e, with tab width 4. Those spans are start 0 end 4 and start 1 end 3. Line 0 returns None. Line 1 returns start 0 end 4. Line 2 returns start 1 end 3. Line 3 returns start 0 end 4. Line 4 returns None. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines.

regression_tests.name: view::fold::tests::innermost_fold_picks_the_inner_span
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because innermost_fold does not exist. Line 0 and line 4 return None. Line 1 and line 3 return the span 0..4. Line 2 returns the span 1..3.
